```text
Lantern Street is a broad pale-paved curved lane between blue timber stalls beneath tall indigo lantern arches. From the Entry Court end, the lift is near-left, one continuous timing-and-supply bench is along the right wall, the mirror alcove is farther left, and the cube canopy and final control are opposite the mirror on the right. Closed Food Street shutters terminate the far bend. A narrow silver moonline follows the physical right paving edge. Preserve these spatial relationships in every view.

Compose a wide from the Entry Court threshold into the lane. Keep the lift recess near-left and the full continuous bench on the right. Let the mirror alcove and opposite cube canopy remain identifiable farther along the bend. The Food Street shutters are shut. All overhead lantern arches are unlit; the narrow moonline is unlit; the five distant indicators are dark. Fixed work lamps provide small warm pools without making the whole street bright. Include one empty parked handcart against the entrance-side stall wall, with its handle projecting slightly towards the lane; this is separate from the lower-store supply cart. Keep fine kit, wheel, tile and cube details too small to read rather than drawing an incorrect solved arrangement. Give the blue timber frontage restrained brass decoration and real depth. The moon is full wherever visible. No Bell, numbered supply shutters, timing drums or floor-mounted mirror square.
```

**Image checks**

- Mirror and cube opposite; moonline on the physical right.
